summary: Defines a padding chunk and a padding parameter for SCTP, with receiver procedures. The chunk pads a packet to any size, and the parameter pads an INIT chunk. This is useful, for example, to probe path MTU.

plainLanguage.summary: SCTP is the transport protocol that carries a phone call or a video stream over a network. This RFC gives it two ways to add filler bytes to a packet, so that a sender can make a packet exactly the size it needs.

questions: how to pad an sctp packet
what is the sctp pad chunk
how to pad an sctp init chunk
subtitle: A chunk and a parameter that let SCTP packets and INIT chunks be enlarged to any size.

tldr.problem: SCTP sometimes needs a packet or an INIT chunk to reach a particular size, for example to match a path MTU, and it had no way to add filler of a chosen length.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a PAD chunk of type 0x84 and a PAD parameter of type 0x8005. Each carries padding data whose length the receiver ignores, and each may be added in multiples of 4 bytes.
tldr.outcome: A sender can now enlarge a packet to an exact size. The receiver simply drops the padding and carries on, and the RFC adds no security considerations of its own.

facts.label: Size a PAD chunk can add

today: RFC 4820 is a Proposed Standard from March 2007, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It adds one chunk type and one INIT parameter type to the SCTP registries, and the use of the PAD chunk for path MTU discovery is described in RFC 4821.

sections.title: Why Pad an SCTP Packet
sections.content:
This document defines a padding chunk and a padding parameter and describes the required receiver side procedures. The padding chunk is used to pad an SCTP packet to an arbitrary size. The padding parameter is used to pad an SCTP INIT chunk to an arbitrary size.

The use of the PAD chunk for path MTU discovery is described in the Packetization Layer Path MTU Discovery document, RFC 4821. The inappropriate use of the PAD parameter or the PAD chunk can result in wasted bandwidth.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes a sender needs its packet to be a particular size, and the only way to get there is to add filler. This RFC defines the filler, in two forms: one that can go in any packet, and one that can only go in the first message of a connection.

sections.title: The Padding Chunk
sections.content:
The PAD chunk pads an SCTP packet. It can enlarge a packet by 4 to 65536 bytes in steps of 4 bytes, and an SCTP packet may contain multiple PAD chunks.

The chunk has a Type field of one byte, which must be set to 0x84 for all PAD chunks. The Flags field is one byte and should be set to zero on transmit and must be ignored on receipt. The Length field is two bytes and holds the length of the padding data plus 4. The padding data itself is the remaining bytes of the chunk and must be ignored by the receiver.
sections.plainLanguage: The chunk header is four bytes: a type byte that says this is padding, a flags byte that is ignored, and a two-byte length counting the filler plus those four bytes. The filler bytes themselves carry no meaning.

sections.title: What the Receiver Does
sections.content:
The receiver of the PAD chunk must discard this chunk and continue processing the rest of the chunks in the packet. The RFC adds that this is also the required processing behaviour for any unknown chunk having the same highest-order two bits of the type as the PAD chunk.

In other words, padding needs no rule of its own. A receiver already knows what to do with a chunk type it does not recognise, and it does the same thing with padding.
sections.plainLanguage: The receiver throws the padding away and reads the rest of the packet as if it had never been there. The RFC says padding is handled the same way as a chunk type the receiver does not recognise, so it needs no separate rule.

sections.title: The Padding Parameter
sections.content:
The PAD parameter pads an INIT chunk, the chunk that opens an SCTP association. It can enlarge the INIT chunk by 4 bytes as the minimum up to the maximum size of the INIT chunk, in steps of 4 bytes, and an INIT chunk may contain multiple PAD parameters.

The parameter has a Parameter Type field of two bytes, which must be set to 0x8005, and a Parameter Length field of two bytes, which holds the length of the padding data plus 4.

The PAD parameter may be included only in the INIT chunk and must not be included in any other chunk. The receiver of the PAD parameter must silently discard it and continue processing the rest of the INIT chunk. This means that the size of the generated COOKIE parameter in the INIT-ACK must not depend on the existence of the PAD parameter in the INIT chunk, and a receiver of a PAD parameter must not include the PAD parameter in any State Cookie parameter it generates. The padding therefore changes the size on the wire without changing the size of the cookie the server sends back.
sections.plainLanguage: The INIT chunk is the first message in an SCTP connection. Padding is only allowed there, and the server must throw it away without letting it change the cookie it sends back, so the reply stays the same size whatever padding arrived.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
A chunk type for the PAD chunk has been assigned by IANA with the value shown in the format above, and has been added to the CHUNK TYPES table of the SCTP parameters registry as 132 (0x84), Padding Chunk (PAD), with this document as the reference.

A parameter type has been assigned for the PAD parameter, and has been added to the CHUNK PARAMETER TYPES table for INIT chunk parameter types as 32773 (0x8005), Padding.
sections.plainLanguage: Two numbers were reserved for this: chunk type 132 and INIT parameter type 32773. They are what the sender and receiver use to recognise the padding.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: This document does not add any additional security considerations to the ones given in RFC 2960.
sections.plainLanguage: Padding adds no new security rules of its own; the rules for SCTP as a whole still apply.

fields.desc: Two bytes, holding the length of the padding data plus 4.
